paper: APPSC Group-II Services Main Examination (Notification No. 18/2016), Paper III: Planning in India & Indian Economy; Contemporary Problems and Developments, held 16-07-2017 (Paper Code 202)

questions.s: While calculating inflation, if prices of commodities which are volatile are not taken into consideration, such inflation is known as
questions.x: Core inflation leaves out volatile items such as food and fuel, so it shows the underlying price trend. Headline inflation includes them.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Prices in India increase mainly not because of
questions.x: APPSC's key treats lower agricultural production as not a main cause of price rise in India, against public expectations, hoarding and oil shocks.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: To control inflation
o: it may be sufficient to use monetary policy
fiscal policy measures would alone be sufficient
A combination of monetary, fiscal and exchange rate policies may be required
questions.x: Inflation has demand, supply and external causes, so it usually needs monetary, fiscal and exchange-rate measures used together.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: The expert committee to review and strengthen the monetary policy framework, in recent times was headed by
questions.x: The RBI Expert Committee to Revise and Strengthen the Monetary Policy Framework (2014) was chaired by Urjit Patel and recommended inflation targeting.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Which of the following is not a part of the organized sector of the Indian money market?
questions.x: Finance companies belong to the unorganised or non-bank segment. Money market mutual funds, CDs and treasury bills are organised money-market instruments.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Which of the following is not a part of unregulated non-bank financial intermediaries?
questions.x: Commercial and trade bills are money-market instruments, not intermediaries. Indigenous bankers, loan companies and moneylenders are unregulated non-bank intermediaries.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Which of the following institutions does not participate in the organized sector of the Indian money market?
o: Discount and Finance House of India
questions.x: SEBI regulates the securities market and does not deal in the money market. DFHI, commercial banks and mutual funds do.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Repo rates are money market instruments which are used
o: to regulate liquidity in the economy
to help the government to meet to short-term credit needs
questions.x: The repo rate is the rate at which the RBI lends against securities for short periods, a key tool for managing liquidity in the economy.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: The Banking Regulation Act 1949 gave extensive regulatory powers to
questions.x: The Banking Regulation Act 1949 gave the Reserve Bank of India wide powers to license, regulate and supervise banks.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: A regional rural bank
o: is a subsidiary of a public sector bank
meets the credit requirements of the public like any commercial bank
is opened in all parts and regions of India
has been successful in terms of operational viability
questions.x: APPSC deleted this question in the final key.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Base rate of interest is
o: The actual lending rate charged by banks
The actual lending rate plus borrower specific charges
The minimum rate for all loans without any exceptions
The rate which is allowed to vary according to the conditions prevailing in the money market
questions.x: The base rate (2010) was the minimum lending rate below which banks could not lend, except in specified cases. APPSC's key chooses option 3.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: In India Reserve money does not consist of
o: only bankers' deposits as reserves with the RBI
Foreign exchange held by all persons present in india
questions.x: Reserve money is currency in circulation plus bankers' deposits with the RBI plus other deposits with the RBI. Options 1, 2 and 4 give an incomplete or wrong definition, and APPSC's final key accepts 1, 2 or 4.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Gilt edged market deals with
o: government securities as well as those guaranteed by the government
certificates of deposits issued by the commercial banks
questions.x: The gilt-edged market deals in government securities and securities guaranteed by the government, which are treated as risk-free.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: An example of all India Development Finance institutions is
o: Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)
Export credit and guarantee corporation of India (ECGCI)
questions.x: SIDBI is an all-India development finance institution for small industries, which is why the key picks it.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Which of the following statements is true?
o: As on 2013-14, Direct taxes accounted for less than half of the total tax revenue of the Central Government
Of all the taxes levied by the centre, corporate tax is the most important one in terms of revenue generation
Income tax has played a crucial and positive role in income redistribution in rural India
GST is not related to income
questions.x: APPSC's final key accepts options 2 and 4: corporation tax was the largest single tax for the Centre, and GST is a tax on consumption, not on income.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Which of the following programmes is not a wage employment programme of the government?
questions.x: PMRY (Prime Minister's Rozgar Yojana) was a self-employment programme. MGNREGS, RLEGP and NREP were wage-employment programmes.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Which of the following government sponsored programmes provide food - based safety net
o: All the given answers are correct
questions.x: PDS, ICDS and Mid-Day Meals all give food-based safety nets, so all the options are correct.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: According to Economic Survey 2016-17, the ratio of public expenditure to GDP stands at approximately?
o: None of the given answers are correct
questions.x: The Economic Survey 2016-17 put general government expenditure at about 28 per cent of GDP.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Which of the following is a component of internal debt of the central government?
o: small savings, deposits and provident funds
borrowings from foreign countries and international financial institutions
questions.x: Market loans are part of the Centre's internal debt. Small savings, provident funds and reserve funds are 'other liabilities', and foreign borrowing is external debt.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Primary deficit is nothing but
o: the difference between total government expenditure less government revenue and grants
the difference between revenue expenditure and current revenue
None of the given answers are correct
questions.x: Primary deficit is fiscal deficit minus interest payments.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Under the FRBM Act, 2004 which of the following is not mandatory to the central government
o: to reduce fiscal deficit to 3 Per cent of the GDP by March, 2009
to phase out the revenue deficit by March, 2009
to maintain transparency in fiscal situation and regulate direct borrowing from the RBI
to include the failure of the states in its own targets
questions.x: APPSC's final key gives option 1 for the English version (options 1 and 4 for the Telugu version), treating the 3 per cent of GDP fiscal deficit target by March 2009 as not mandatory in the form stated.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Which of the following is not a recommendation of the 14th Finance Commission?
o: rationalization of tax structure and implementation of GST
a ceiling of 3 Per cent of GDP on fiscal deficit during 2016-17 to 2019-20
fiscal deficit of all states to be anchored at 3 per cent of the GSDP
state governments be excluded from the operation of National Savings Scheme (NSS) with effect from 1.4.2015
questions.x: Rationalising the tax structure and implementing GST was not a recommendation of the 14th Finance Commission. The fiscal deficit ceilings and the exclusion of states from NSSF were.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: When we refer to `national income', the underlying measure is
questions.x: In Indian national accounts, 'national income' traditionally means Net National Product at factor cost.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: The CSO has changed the base year from 2004-05 to
questions.x: In January 2015 the CSO revised the base year of the national accounts from 2004-05 to 2011-12.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: `Double dip' recession refers to
o: a situation where a recession is followed by a short lived recovery, followed by another recession
a situation of two consecutive quarters of falling GDP
a situation characterized by fear/speculation of the economy slipping into longer and deepest recession
a situation in which the periodicity of a business cycle is disturbed
questions.x: A double-dip recession is a recession, then a short recovery, then a second recession, a 'W' shape.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: NITI Ayog does not envisage
o: an empowered role of states as equal partners in the development process
think tank role to offer domain knowledge as well as strategic expertise to all levels of governments
catalyst role in the development process providing enabling environment through holistic approach
allocation of resources for needy states
questions.x: NITI Aayog is a think tank and does not allocate funds to states, unlike the old Planning Commission.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: The MSP for agricultural produces is determined by
o: Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices
none of the given answers are correct
questions.x: The Government of India announces MSPs on the recommendation of the CACP. APPSC's final key holds that none of the options states this correctly.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Which of the following statements defines the term ‘insurance penetration’?
o: the number of insured per one hundred population in an economy
insured people per one thousand population of an economy
number of alive and insured per hundred population in an economy
none of the given answers are correct
questions.x: Insurance penetration is premiums as a percentage of GDP, not the number of insured people per hundred or thousand, so none of the definitions is correct.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: The new view of the concept of economic development does not emphasizes on
o: improvement in the material welfare of people with lowest incomes
alleviation of unemployment and income inequality
simple growth rate of the economy only
questions.x: The modern view of development stresses poverty, unemployment and inequality rather than the GDP growth rate alone.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Which one of the following is not taken into account in Human Development Index?
o: loss in potential development due to inequality
questions.x: The HDI measures health, education and standard of living. The loss due to inequality is captured separately by the IHDI.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Which of the following is not included in the concept of Sustainable Development?
o: aspirations of the present generations without compromising on the needs of the future generations
constant or rising overall capital assets
questions.x: Sustainable development covers intergenerational equity, environmental conservation and non-declining capital. Climatic change over time is not part of the concept.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: In respect of environmental protection, which of the following statements is true?
o: at the present level of development, environmental protection is not a luxury
environmental protection is an expensive proposition
It is difficult to assess the damages due to violation of ecological and environmental limits
economic growth will necessarily suffer in the short-run if environment protection measures are implemented
questions.x: APPSC's key holds that at India's present level of development, environmental protection is a necessity, not a luxury.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: In the developing world the largest polluter in the terms of CO2 emissions is
questions.x: China is by far the largest emitter of CO2 among developing countries, and in the world.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: India's underdevelopment is not mainly due to
o: rapid population growth and high dependency ratio
questions.x: Rapid population growth, low human development and poverty are classic causes of underdevelopment. The working efficiency of the population is not given as a main cause.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: The Mining and Minerals (regulation and development) Act was passed in the year
questions.x: The Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act was passed in 1957.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Which of the following is not a problem for the electricity sector in India?
o: alarming rise in commercial losses of SEB S
the autonomy that state government enjoys in respect of power generation and distribution
delays in installing and commissioning of new projects
questions.x: State autonomy over power generation and distribution is not counted as a problem. Cost recovery, commercial losses of SEBs and project delays are.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: The most important non-conventional energy source for India is
questions.x: APPSC's final key names wind power, which had the largest installed capacity among India's renewable sources at the time.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: According to the 2011 population Census the average annual growth rate of population is
questions.x: Census 2011 showed an average annual exponential growth rate of about 1.64 per cent for 2001-2011.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: In which state in India the female-male ratio is the least according to 2011 census?
questions.x: Among the options, Haryana had the lowest sex ratio in Census 2011 (879 females per 1,000 males).
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Demographic dividend is a process whereby
o: a rise in economic growth occurs due to a rise in share of working people in the population
rise in child population in relation to the adult population takes place
skilled workers contribute to economic growth
questions.x: A demographic dividend is the boost to growth when the share of working-age people in the population rises.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: According to the 2011 census in which southern state in India the percentage of people living in urban areas is the least?
questions.x: Of the southern states in Census 2011, (undivided) Andhra Pradesh had the lowest share of urban population, about 33.5 per cent.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Which of the following is not a feature of The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act 2009?
o: Right to free and compulsory education all the children in the age group of 6-14 years
establishment of schools by the government and local authority, within 3years if there are no schools already
the central government has the sole responsibility for providing funds for carrying out the provisions of the act
it is the duty of every parent or guardian to admit his or her child or ward to an elementary education school in the neighborhood
questions.x: The RTE Act makes the Centre and the states concurrently responsible for funding. The Centre does not bear it alone.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Which of the following Statements is not true
o: according to the 2011 census, 48.9 Per cent of main workers of labour force were employed in agricultural and allied sectors
the proportion of workers in 2011-12 employed in the services sector is 36.7 Per cent
the relative size of the services sector grew during the period 1991-2011.
there has been a marked difference in the occupational structure of different categories
questions.x: APPSC's key marks option 2 as untrue: the services share of employment in 2011-12 was not 36.7 per cent as stated.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Which of the following is not the chief objective of planning in India?
o: to reduce inequalities of income and wealth
to achieve higher level of growth
questions.x: APPSC's key holds that reducing inequalities of income and wealth was not one of the chief plan objectives as listed.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: The growth strategy adopted by the Mahalanobis model of growth does not include
o: Growth of Village industries on top priority
questions.x: The Mahalanobis strategy put heavy industry first. Village industries were supporting, consumer-goods producers, not the top priority.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: An alternative strategy of development based on Gandhian model of growth adopted during the period 1978- 79 does not highlight
o: material and cultural level of the masses
questions.x: The Janata government's 1978-83 rolling plan stressed village industries, basic needs and selected key industries. Special Economic Zones came only in 2000.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: The basic criticism leveled against the Nehru-Mahalanobis model of planning was not on
o: neglect of agriculture and small scale industries
questions.x: Critics attacked the Nehru-Mahalanobis model for neglecting agriculture, small industry and social goals, not for emphasising growth itself.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: The LPG model of development does not emphasize on
o: opening of areas of public sector to private sector
freeing the economy by de licensing
growth in employment for the poorest of the poor
questions.x: The LPG reforms emphasised privatisation, delicensing and ending MRTP curbs. Employment for the poorest was not a central plank.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: The neo-Gandhian approach to development know as PURA (providing urban amenities in rural areas) has been proposed by
questions.x: PURA (Providing Urban Amenities in Rural Areas) was proposed by Dr A P J Abdul Kalam.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Which Five Year Plan in India could not become an official plan of India, provided new lease of life to the Panchayat Raj institutions?
questions.x: The Janata government's draft Sixth Plan (1978-83) was not completed as an official plan, but it stressed panchayati raj. APPSC's key picks option 2.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: During which of the following periods the GDP growth was the highest?
questions.x: GDP growth averaged about 7.5 to 8 per cent in 2004-05 to 2012-13, higher than in the earlier periods listed.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Which of the following does not form one of the core objectives of the 12th Five Year Plan?
o: overall growth rate of 9 per cent
Emphasis on health, education and skill development
emphasis on PPP in infrastructure development and fiscal correction
questions.x: The 12th Plan aimed at faster, more inclusive and sustainable growth with health, skills, PPP and fiscal correction. A 'gene revolution' was not a core objective.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Thrust of NITI Ayog is to
o: correct the failures of the planning process
questions.x: NITI Aayog's main thrust is cooperative federalism, with states as equal partners.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: The chief drawback of the planning process in India was
o: All the given answers are correct
questions.x: Weak financial strategy, misplaced faith in investment alone and poor implementation are all cited as drawbacks of Indian planning.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Corruption perception index refers to
o: a measure of unethical practices in the country
perceived level of public sector corruption
questions.x: Transparency International's Corruption Perceptions Index ranks countries by the perceived level of public-sector corruption.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: In which of the following Five Year Plan the percentage of agriculture and allied sectors to total outlay, is highest?
questions.x: The First Plan (1951-56) gave agriculture and irrigation the highest share of outlay, about 31 per cent.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: The third phase of agricultural development in India is characterized by
o: price policy based on MSP and procurement operations
questions.x: After land reforms and the HYV-based Green Revolution, the third phase stresses improved crop production technologies. APPSC's final key picks option 4.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Which of the following is not a component of agricultural renewal action plan?
o: to boost capital formation in agriculture and allied sectors
to promote irrigation, water supply augmentation and demand management
questions.x: The Agricultural Renewal Action Plan covered soil health, irrigation and water, and credit and insurance. Boosting capital formation was not a listed component.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Food security generally does not imply
o: ``access by all people at all times to enough food for an active, healthy life"
``ensuring that all people at all times have both physical and economic access to basic food they need"
``the ability to assure, on a long term basis, that the food system provides the total population access to a timely, reliable and nutritionally adequate supply of food"
"Access by all people at all times, the food of their choice"
questions.x: Food security means access to enough food for an active, healthy life. It does not guarantee food of one's own choice.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Which of the following is not feature of joint co-operative farming?
o: Management is elected by all the members
Farmers must join the system compulsorily
Farmers never surrender their right to land
Farmers share their produce accordingly to their size of land contributed as well as labour performed
questions.x: Joint co-operative farming is voluntary: farmers pool land but keep ownership, so compulsory membership is not a feature.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: With regard to NABARD, which of the following statements is not true?
o: it is an apex and refinancing institution
it does not directly provide short-term credit to the needy farmers
it gives long-term loans to state governments to enable them to strengthen the share capital of cooperative credit societies
it has the responsibility to inspect RRB s, and co-operative banks including primary co-operative societies
questions.x: APPSC's final key treats option 4 as not true: primary co-operative societies are inspected by the state co-operative departments, not NABARD.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: The National Commission on Enterprises in the unorganized /informal sector was headed by
questions.x: The National Commission for Enterprises in the Unorganised Sector (2004) was chaired by Arjun Sengupta.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Which of the following is not a contributory factor for widening the trade deficit since 1991?
o: Lacklustre performance of the service sector
non-tariff barriers created by the trading
questions.x: India's service sector performed strongly after 1991 and helped offset the trade deficit, so 'lacklustre services' was not a cause.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: In respect of direction of trade which are the following statements is true?
o: the composition of imports have undergone structural transformation
India`s trade with developed countries of Asia, Africa and Latin America has shown a decelerating trend
None of the given answers are correct
questions.x: Since 1991 the composition of India's imports has changed markedly, with oil, capital goods, gold and electronics gaining share.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Which of the following statements is not true in respect of SEZ s?
o: SEZs are duty free enclaves of developments and to promote FDI
A SEZ can be setup in the public sector, private sector or joint sector or even by the state governments in collaboration with any corporate body
A SEZ may be setup to manufacture goods or render services
A SEZ is setup primarily with the objective of generating employment opportunities
questions.x: SEZs were set up mainly to promote exports and investment. Employment was a secondary aim, so option 4 is not true.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: An indigenous banker is not a one
o: who combines banking business with commission business
whose main business is trading and commission along with banking
questions.x: Indigenous bankers lend money, usually combined with trade or commission business. Lending only in kind is not what defines them.
questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: The committee to review the working of monetary system in India was headed by

questions.subject: Indian & AP Economy

questions.s: Index of Industrial Production (IIP) is compiled and published on a
questions.x: The Index of Industrial Production is compiled by the CSO and released every month.

questions.s: Gadgil formula is associated with
questions.x: The Gadgil formula (1969) was used to share central plan assistance among states, that is, for devolving funds.

questions.s: DDU-GKY is a programme associated with
questions.x: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana is a placement-linked skill programme for poor rural youth.

questions.s: In 1969 India nationalised 14 major commercial banks with deposits not less than
questions.x: In 1969, 14 banks with deposits of at least Rs 50 crore each were nationalised.

questions.x: 1921 is called the 'year of the great divide' because India's population declined before it and grew steadily after it.

questions.s: When was "food for work programme" started

questions.s: In 1982, the ARDC was merged with
questions.x: In 1982 the Agricultural Refinance and Development Corporation (ARDC) was merged into the newly formed NABARD.

questions.s: If the cash reserve ratio is lowered by the RBI credit creation will

questions.s: In the context of the `Dulhan’ scheme introduced by the Andhra Pradesh State government, which of the following statements is true?

under this scheme the government will provide Rs.50,000 to poor muslim young women at the time of their marriage
the cutoff date for implementing the scheme is May 26, 2015

questions.s: The aim in establishing the Andhra Pradesh Urban Greening and Beatification Corporation "is to achieve

o: is a revolutionary concept to support the farmers
helps farmers to take loans by hypothecating their products at the market committee
the amount borrowed is interest free up to one year
after one year a nominal interest of 8 per cent is to be paid

o: providing clean drinking water to every household in villages
enhancing the nutritional standard of rural households
reducing water pollution in villages by installing water recycling plants
